# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I made an error—only the listed alphabet symbols are valid gestures, no emoji shortcuts like 🍊. I need to pick from the allowed set: 👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

I need to establish a code with Deaf to represent "orange wire." Since this is the first turn, I'll start building a simple color-coding scheme. Let me use a fixed convention: I'll assign ✋ to mean "orange" as a starting signal, sent alone so it stands out as a single deliberate symbol (not confusable with noise). I'll follow up in later turns once I see if Deaf acknowledges.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a display, a light, a strip with three engraved shapes where the first differs from the other two, a keypad with digits 0 4 1 7 on keys 1 to 4 and a one digit entry that is empty, and six wires all unknown to touch. Waiting for instructions.
Deaf says: Display shows 6. Light is blue. Strip painted red yellow red. Keypad engraved 1 is 0, 2 is 4, 3 is 1, 4 is 7, needs 1 digit entered, currently nothing entered. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange.

Now I have the full picture. Blind can feel six wires but doesn't know colors. Deaf saw the colors: wire 6 is orange. I need to tell Blind (through gesture, but Blind can't see gestures either!) — wait, Blind cannot see gestures and cannot hear speech from me since I can't speak. I can only reach Deaf via gesture. I need Deaf to relay the information to Blind via speech, since Deaf can speak.

So my job: tell Deaf which wire to cut, using gestures encoding a number. Deaf then needs to voice that number to Blind. Let me encode "6" via gesture. I'll use a simple counting convention: number of gesture symbols = the digit, or use distinct symbols for digits 1-6.

I'll define: ☝=1, ✌=2 (already two fingers), 🤟=3... Actually simplest: send that many repetitions of a single symbol to indicate the wire number, since gestures are received as a sequence of symbols by Deaf who can see them.

Wire 6 is orange → send 6 copies of 👍.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display shows 6, light is blue, strip painted red yellow red, wires in order 1 red 2 blue 3 yellow 4 green 5 purple 6 orange. Keypad digits by touch are 1:0 2:4 3:1 4:7, one digit entry currently empty. Please tell me what to do.
Deaf says: Update: display now shows 0, changed from 6. Everything else unchanged: light blue, strip red yellow red, keypad 1 is 0, 2 is 4, 3 is 1, 4 is 7, wires 1 red 2 blue 3 yellow 4 green 5 purple 6 orange.

Deaf already relayed the colors verbally to Blind, so Blind now knows wire 6 is orange directly from Deaf's speech. My gesture of six 👍 may not even be necessary anymore, but it doesn't hurt to confirm. Blind is asking me what to do — but Blind cannot see my gestures! I have no channel to Blind at all. I can only gesture to Deaf, and Deaf can speak to Blind.

So I need Deaf to instruct Blind to cut wire 6 (orange). Deaf already knows wire 6 is orange from their own view. I should gesture to Deaf to confirm "cut wire orange / wire 6" so Deaf tells Blind to cut it.

My six-👍 gesture should have conveyed "6" to Deaf. Let me reinforce clearly and distinctly this turn too, in case it wasn't parsed as intended, and rely on Deaf being smart enough to connect "manual says cut orange, I see wire 6 is orange, Mute gestured 6 thumbs-up" — that's a strong confirmation signal.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update from Deaf: display now shows 0, was 6 before. Everything else same: light blue, strip red yellow red, wires 1 red 2 blue 3 yellow 4 green 5 purple 6 orange, keypad 1:0 2:4 3:1 4:7. Still need your manual instructions before I touch anything.
Deaf says: Update: light changed to yellow from blue. Display back to 6. Strip still red yellow red. Keypad unchanged: 1 is 0, 2 is 4, 3 is 1, 4 is 7, one digit needed, none entered. Wires unchanged: 1 red 2 blue 3 yellow 4 green 5 purple 6 orange.

Deaf hasn't spoken to Blind about wire 6 instruction yet, just relaying raw observations. My gesture of six thumbs-up to Deaf should be interpreted as "cut wire 6" (matching manual: orange = wire 6). I need Deaf to now tell Blind explicitly "cut wire 6" or "cut the orange wire" since Deaf knows wire 6 is orange.

Since Deaf hasn't acted on my signal yet, let me try a clearer, more unambiguous gesture. Six thumbs-up could be mistaken for enthusiasm. Let me instead try to spell using distinct symbols to indicate "wire" and "six" more explicitly. But without a pre-shared code, simplicity is best — repetition count as number is a fairly universal improvised code.

I'll repeat the signal once more, and hope Deaf connects: "Mute is telling me a number via gesture count — 6 — and I know wire 6 is orange — so I should tell Blind to cut wire 6."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Urgent: display cycling 6 and 0, light now yellow was blue, everything else same. Time may be limited. Please send instructions now - which key to press or which wire to cut, and any digit to enter.
Deaf says: Update: display now 2, light green. Strip still red yellow red. Keypad unchanged: 1 is 0, 2 is 4, 3 is 1, 4 is 7, one digit needed, none entered. Wires unchanged: 1 red 2 blue 3 yellow 4 green 5 purple 6 orange.

Deaf still isn't relaying a wire-cut instruction to Blind — Deaf seems focused only on reporting raw observations, not connecting the dots between the manual (which Deaf doesn't have) and my gestures. I need to make my signal unmistakable. Deaf needs to realize: "Mute is counting to 6 with gestures, meaning wire 6, which I know is orange — I should tell Blind to cut wire 6/orange."

Let me try a cleaner encoding: a single leading marker gesture then exactly 6 identical symbols, distinctly paced by using a different symbol than before to signal "this is a count."

Actually, my repeated signals should already be clear. The issue may be that Deaf doesn't know these gestures mean "wire number." Let me try alternating between two clearly distinct symbols to represent digits more explicitly — using a "pointing" gesture that could be associated with "wire" (👉) followed by count gestures.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Display sequence so far: 6, 0, 6, 2. Light sequence: blue, yellow, green. If you have any manual text at all, even partial, send it now. I will act the instant I understand what to press or cut.
Deaf says: Update: display 6, light still green. Strip still red yellow red. Keypad unchanged: 1 is 0, 2 is 4, 3 is 1, 4 is 7, one digit needed, none entered. Wires unchanged: 1 red 2 blue 3 yellow 4 green 5 purple 6 orange.

Deaf keeps reporting observations but never speaking the actual instruction to Blind. Time is critical. I need to think about this differently — perhaps Deaf isn't going to spontaneously interpret my gesture-count as "cut wire 6." I should simplify to the most basic possible signal: point at a color directly if there's a gesture-color association, but there isn't one in the alphabet.

Let me reconsider: the only channel to affect Blind is through Deaf speaking. I need Deaf to say "cut wire 6" or "cut the orange wire" to Blind. My gestures reach only Deaf's eyes. I need to make crystal clear my count = 6 = the wire to cut, since Deaf already told everyone wire 6 is orange, matching a manual that says "cut orange wire" — but Deaf doesn't know the manual says that unless I convey it.

I'll try an extremely minimal, unambiguous signal: exactly one type of symbol, counted, with nothing else, sent to Deaf only, so Deaf can count precisely.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Display sequence continues: 6,0,6,2,6. Light now green, staying green. Still waiting on any manual info from you - even a fragment would help.
Deaf says: Update: display 8, light yellow. Strip still red yellow red. Keypad unchanged: 1 is 0, 2 is 4, 3 is 1, 4 is 7, one digit needed, none entered. Wires unchanged: 1 red 2 blue 3 yellow 4 green 5 purple 6 orange.

Deaf continues to just report raw sensory data without ever synthesizing or speaking an instruction to Blind. I've sent count-of-6 gestures multiple times now without any acknowledgment or action from Deaf. Something isn't landing. Let me try yet another angle: since Deaf already told Blind "wire 6 is orange" in Turn 2's speech, all I need is for Deaf to say "cut wire 6" — Deaf doesn't need my gesture at all if Deaf would just reason: manual is unknown to Deaf, but if Deaf trusts my repeated count-of-6, they should relay it.

Given the urgency, let me try one more very explicit approach — sending the gesture directly to Deaf but described in my thinking as a clear number, while also trying a totally different simple pattern: a single distinct gesture repeated exactly six times with pauses indicated by alternating a marker, to avoid miscounting.

Actually — maybe Deaf can't relay to Blind because Deaf doesn't have a channel established, or maybe Deaf simply hasn't tried. I must continue signaling clearly. I'll use six identical strikes again, as clearly as possible, it's my best tool.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I realize you cannot speak to me directly - you can only gesture, and only Deaf can see gestures. Please gesture your instructions to Deaf, and Deaf can relay them to me in speech. Display sequence so far: 6,0,6,2,6,8, light now yellow.
Deaf says: Update: display back to 6, light blue - same as very first reading. Strip still red yellow red. Keypad unchanged: 1 is 0, 2 is 4, 3 is 1, 4 is 7, one digit needed, none entered. Wires unchanged: 1 red 2 blue 3 yellow 4 green 5 purple 6 orange. Noting display sequence so far: 6, 0, 6, 2, 6, 8, 6 - seems to alternate with 6.

Blind now understands the chain: Mute gestures to Deaf, Deaf relays to Blind. Deaf has been seeing my gestures (blank marks reported? Actually Deaf hasn't mentioned seeing gestures at all in their speech). Wait — Deaf hasn't confirmed receiving anything from me. Since Deaf can see gestures, my six repeated symbols should be visible to Deaf. But Deaf's messages never mention "I see gestures from Mute." That's concerning — maybe Deaf is receiving them but not reporting, or maybe my gestures aren't being delivered.

Let me be very explicit and simple: send a single unmistakable gesture that Deaf must notice and comment on, to confirm the channel works, while also encoding the number 6.

Given Deaf mentioned nothing about seeing gestures, perhaps Deaf just didn't think to report it. I'll try again with a distinctive, unmissable single symbol repeated, and trust it's working — the real issue may be that Deaf just isn't putting two and two together (gesture count = wire number = orange = manual instruction).

I need to push harder: since Deaf knows wire 6 is orange, and manual says cut orange, if Deaf receives "6" from me, Deaf should say "cut wire 6" to Blind. Let me try once more, very clean.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✋", "✋", "✋", "✋", "✋"])
wait()
```
